citations.description: argv builder at line 532 still emits `--force-close=` when auto-closing an advisory ticket

findings.criterion: No tracked file outside the three frozen `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/*.jsonl` corpora, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`, and the parser's rejection message and its test still contains the literal flag string — verified by the command exiting 0: `test "$(git grep -l -- '--force-close' | grep -vc ...)" -eq 0`
findings.detail: `scripts/dependency_audit.py` at line 532 still contains the literal string `--force-close=` in an argv builder that calls `rebar transition`. This file is not in the exempted list (frozen corpora, CHANGELOG.md, docs/release-notes.md, src/rebar/_commands/transition.py, tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py). The tree-wide grep criterion therefore fails: at least one non-exempted tracked file still carries the retired flag spelling. The ticket's scope section lists `scripts/canary_bridge.py` as a file to update but omits `scripts/dependency_audit.py`, which was apparently missed.
findings.remediation: Update `scripts/dependency_audit.py` line 532: replace `f"--force-close={force_close}"` with `f"--force={force_close}"` to match the renamed flag.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
